data.content_ref: inline:The refutation condition is self-defeating rather than properly falsifying the claimed inheritance. The claim says causal firebreaks are an implementation of the modular-DAG requirement. A genuine counterexample would show firebreaks operating without enforcing a DAG (e.g., firebreaks that suppress cascading failures in a cyclic topology). Instead, the refutation condition concedes 'cascading failures' persist despite the firebreaks—which means the firebreaks are not functioning as firebreaks, not that they function independently of the DAG requirement. Failing to refute a claim by restating the claim's own failure mode is not a substantive relation, it is circular.
